newsitem.title: UK: GOLF-FURYK, CLARKE LEAD BRITISH OPEN WITH 67S.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-FURYK, CLARKE LEAD BRITISH OPEN WITH 67S.

text.p: Tiger Woods shot 72 in the British Open on Thursday as wild-swinging American Jim Furyk and powerful Northern Irishman Darren Clarke both tamed Royal Troon's tough back nine to lead with four-under-par 67s.

The Masters champion's round included a triple-bogey at the 11th hole after he drove into a gorse bush, took a penalty drop, half-fluffed his third, struck an eight iron over the green, chipped and two-putted.
Some of the sport's biggest names also struggled on the windy course on the south west coast of Scotland.
Local favourite Colin Montgomerie, who has missed four of the last five British Open cuts, went to pieces on the course where he played as a boy.
The U.S. Open runner-up could not stop blocking his tee shots to the right and hit only the first three fairways in a disappointing five-over-par 76.
Worse was to come from former Open champion Ian Baker-Finch who slumped to a disastrous 92 -- 21-over -- and later withdrew from the Open.
It was a day when Woods proved he has the mental strength to match his obvious power and class.
"My plan was to be patient and I didn't lose it. Frustrated at the 11th, yes, lose patience, no," the 21-year-old said. "I maintained it all day and I'm definitely proud of that."
Birdies at the 16th and 18th from 15 and 18 feet hauled him back into contention.

Furyk and Clarke each played the back nine, which lived up to its fearsome reputation, in level-par 35 in a strong wind to snatch a two-stroke lead over world number three Greg Norman and Americans Fred Couples and Justin Leonard.
Four more players shot 70 and five more including five-times champion Tom Watson and three-times winner Nick Faldo had level-par 71s.
U.S. Open champion Ernie Els carded a three-over-par 75 while titleholder Tom Lehman shot 74.
Furyk, 27, has a swing described as being "like a man trying to kill a snake in a phone booth." After six consecutive top-10 finishes on the U.S. Tour, he came here confident of playing well.
Four birdies in the front nine, one at the short eighth from 35 feet, were followed by another at the 11th, Woods's triple bogey hole.

Clarke, a consistent player certain to make Europe's Ryder Cup team this year, birdied four of the first seven holes and another at the 11th where he sank a 70-foot putt from the front edge of the green.
He is not sure of being ready to win a major championship.
"I would like to get myself into contention first, and take the next step from there," he said.
Norman, the 1986 and 1993 champion, and 1992 Masters champion Couples revelled on the downwind front nine and then survived coming back into the wind.
Norman played the front nine in four-under 32 and the back in two-over 37 while Couples, whose father is seriously ill with leukaemia, shot 31-38 for his 69.
"We are playing two different golf courses out there," said Norman, who dropped shots at the 13th and the last. "The wind is heavy and it is very cold. Coming home you have to hang on.
American Davis Love and Angel Cabrera of Argentina were in the group on 70 with two-times U.S. Open champion Curtis Strange and Ian Woosnam of Britain also on 71.
Watson did not hit any greens in regulation figures in his back nine of 38 but chipped well to limit the damage.
"I didn't put myself out of play. That's what you have to do on this golf course," he said. "Everybody knows what the wind is like. The back nine is one of the toughest nines in golf."
Montgomerie, winner of the Irish Open after a closing 62 this month, looked a bit shell-shocked after his 76.
"I've done badly in British Opens before. Whether I do well tomorrow or not, I'll come back from this and it won't hurt," he said.
